longTitle.officialTitle: To authorize appropriations for fiscal year 2012 for military activities of the Department of Defense, for military construction, and for defense activities of the Department of Energy, to prescribe military personnel strengths for such fiscal year, and for other purposes.

main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012”.

section.heading: ORGANIZATION OF ACT INTO DIVISIONS; TABLE OF CONTENTS.

subsection.heading: Divisions.—
subsection.chapeau: This Act is organized into five divisions as follows:

paragraph.content: Division A—Department of Defense Authorizations.
Division B—Military Construction Authorizations.
Division C—Department of Energy National Security Authorizations and Other Authorizations.
Division D—Funding Tables.
Division E—SBIR and STTR Reauthorization.

subsection.heading: Table of Contents.—
subsection.content:

section.heading: AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.
section.content: Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2012 for procurement for the Army, the Navy and the Marine Corps, the Air Force, and Defense-wide activities, as specified in the funding table in section 4101.

section.heading: LIMITATION ON PROCUREMENT OF STRYKER COMBAT VEHICLES.

subsection.heading: Limitation.—
subsection.content: Except as provided by subsection (b), of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2012 for weapons and tracked combat vehicles, Army, the Secretary of the Army may not procure more than 100 Stryker combat vehicles.

subsection.heading: Waiver.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of the Army may waive the limitation under subsection (a) if the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees written certification by the Assistant Secretary of the Army for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics that—

paragraph.content: there are validated needs of the Army requiring the waiver;
all Stryker combat vehicles required to fully equip the nine Stryker brigades and to meet other validated requirements regarding the vehicle have been procured or placed on contract for procurement;
the size of the Stryker combat vehicle fleet not assigned directly to Stryker brigade combat teams is essential to maintaining the readiness of Stryker brigade combat teams; and
with respect to the Stryker combat vehicles planned to be procured pursuant to the waiver, cost estimates are complete for the long-term sustainment of the vehicles.

section.heading: LIMITATION ON RETIREMENT OF C-23 AIRCRAFT.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Upon determining to retire a C-23 aircraft for which there has been no previously agreed upon transfer of title for such aircraft as of the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Army shall first offer title to such aircraft to the chief executive officer of the State in which such aircraft is based.

subsection.heading: Transfer Upon Acceptance of Offer.—
subsection.content: If the chief executive officer of a State accepts title of an aircraft under subsection (a), the Secretary shall transfer title of the aircraft to the State without charge to the State. The Secretary shall provide a reasonable amount of time for acceptance of the offer.

subsection.heading: Sustainment.—
subsection.content: Immediately upon transfer of title to an aircraft to the State under this section, the State shall assume all costs associated with operating, maintaining, sustaining, and modernizing the aircraft.

paragraph.heading: Study.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Air Force, in consultation with the Secretary of the Army, the Director of the National Guard Bureau, each supported commander of a combatant command, and the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, shall conduct a study to determine the number of fixed-wing and rotary-wing aircraft required to support the following titles 10 and 32, United States Code, missions at low, medium, moderate, high, and very-high levels of operational risk:

subparagraph.content: Homeland defense.
Time sensitive, direct support to forces consisting of the regular component of the Army and the National Guard.
Disaster response.
Humanitarian assistance.

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report containing the study under paragraph (1).

paragraph.heading: Review.—
paragraph.content: The Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a sufficiency review of the study under subsection (d)(1).

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.content: The Comptroller General shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report containing the review under paragraph (1).

section.heading: MULTIYEAR PROCUREMENT AUTHORITY FOR AIRFRAMES FOR ARMY UH-60M/HH-60M HELICOPTERS AND NAVY MH-60R/MH-60S HELICOPTERS.

subsection.heading: Authority for Multiyear Procurement.—
subsection.content: Subject to section 2306b of title 10, United States Code, the Secretary of the Army may enter into one or more multiyear contracts, beginning with the fiscal year 2012 program year, for the procurement of airframes for UH-60M/HH-60M helicopters and, acting as the executive agent for the Department of the Navy, for the procurement of airframes for MH-60R/S helicopters.

subsection.heading: Condition for Out-year Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: A contract entered into under subsection (a) shall provide that any obligation of the United States to make a payment under the contract for a fiscal year after fiscal year 2012 is subject to the availability of appropriations for that purpose for such later fiscal year.

section.heading: MULTIYEAR PROCUREMENT AUTHORITY FOR MISSION AVIONICS AND COMMON COCKPITS FOR NAVY MH-60R/S HELICOPTERS.

subsection.heading: Authority for Multiyear Procurement.—
subsection.content: Subject to section 2306b of title 10, United States Code, the Secretary of the Navy may enter into one or more multiyear contracts, beginning with the fiscal year 2012 program year, for the procurement of mission avionics and common cockpits for MH-60R/S helicopters.

subsection.heading: Condition for Out-year Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: A contract entered into under subsection (a) shall provide that any obligation of the United States to make a payment under the contract for a fiscal year after fiscal year 2012 is subject to the availability of appropriations for that purpose for such later fiscal year.

section.heading: SEPARATE PROCUREMENT LINE ITEM FOR CERTAIN LITTORAL COMBAT SHIP MISSION MODULES.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: In the budget materials submitted to the President by the Secretary of Defense in connection with the submission to Congress, pursuant to section 1105 of title 31, United States Code, of the budget for fiscal year 2013, and each subsequent fiscal year, the Secretary shall ensure that a separate, dedicated procurement line item is designated for each covered module that includes the quantity and cost of each such module requested.

subsection.heading: Form.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall ensure that any classified components of covered modules not included in a procurement line item under subsection (a) shall be included in a classified annex.

subsection.heading: Covered Module.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section, the term “covered module” means, with respect to mission modules of the Littoral Combat Ship, the following modules:

paragraph.content: Surface warfare.
Mine countermeasures.
Anti-submarine warfare.

section.heading: LIFE-CYCLE COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS ON ALTERNATIVE MAINTENANCE AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANS FOR THE LITTORAL COMBAT SHIP PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: Cost-benefit Analysis.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Navy shall conduct a life-cycle cost-benefit analysis, in accordance with the Office of Management and Budget Circular A-94, comparing alternative maintenance and sustainability plans for the Littoral Combat Ship program.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: At the same time that the budget of the President is submitted to Congress under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code, for fiscal year 2013, the Secretary of the Navy shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the cost-benefit analysis conducted under subsection (a).

section.heading: EXTENSION OF FORD-CLASS AIRCRAFT CARRIER CONSTRUCTION AUTHORITY.
section.content: Section 121(a) of the John Warner National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2007 (Public Law 109-364; 120 Stat. 2104) is amended by striking “three fiscal years” and inserting “four fiscal years”.

section.heading: STRATEGIC AIRLIFT AIRCRAFT FORCE STRUCTURE.
section.chapeau: Section 8062(g)(1) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.content: by striking “October 1, 2009” and inserting “October 1, 2011”; and
by striking “316 aircraft” and inserting “301 aircraft”.

section.heading: LIMITATIONS ON USE OF FUNDS TO RETIRE B-1 BOMBER AIRCRAFT.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act for fiscal year 2012 for the Department of Defense may be obligated or expended to retire any B-1 bomber aircraft on or before the date on which the Secretary of the Air Force submits to the congressional defense committees the plan described in subsection (b).

subsection.heading: Plan Described.—
subsection.chapeau: The plan described in this subsection is a plan for retiring B-1 bomber aircraft that includes the following:

paragraph.content: An identification of each B-1 bomber aircraft that will be retired and the disposition plan for such aircraft.
An estimate of the savings that will result from the proposed retirement of B-1 bomber aircraft in each calendar year through calendar year 2022.

An estimate of the amount of the savings described in paragraph (2) that will be reinvested in the modernization of B-1 bomber aircraft still in service in each calendar year through calendar year 2022.
A modernization plan for sustaining the remaining B-1 bomber aircraft through at least calendar year 2022.
An estimate of the amount of funding required to fully fund the modernization plan described in paragraph (4) for each calendar year through calendar year 2022.
paragraph.editorialNote: [Section 133 was repealed by section 136(d) of Public Law 115–91.]

section.heading: AVAILABILITY OF FISCAL YEAR 2011 FUNDS FOR RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT RELATING TO THE B-2 BOMBER AIRCRAFT.
section.content: Of the unobligated balance of amounts appropriated for fiscal year 2011 for the Air Force and available for procurement of B-2 bomber aircraft modifications, post-production support, and other charges, $20,000,000 may be available for fiscal year 2012 for research, development, test, and evaluation with respect to a conventional mixed load capability for the B-2 bomber aircraft.

section.heading: AVAILABILITY OF FISCAL YEAR 2011 FUNDS TO SUPPORT ALTERNATIVE OPTIONS FOR EXTREMELY HIGH FREQUENCY TERMINAL INCREMENT 1 PROGRAM OF RECORD.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Of the unobligated balance of amounts appropriated for fiscal year 2011 for the Air Force and available for procurement of B-2 bomber aircraft modifications, post-production support, and other charges, $15,000,000 may be available to support alternative options for the extremely high frequency terminal Increment 1 program of record.

subsection.heading: Plan To Secure Protected Communications.—
subsection.content: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Air Force shall submit to the congressional defense committees a plan to provide an extremely high frequency terminal for secure protected communications for the B-2 bomber aircraft and other aircraft.

section.heading: PROCUREMENT OF ADVANCED EXTREMELY HIGH FREQUENCY SATELLITES.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary of the Air Force may procure two advanced extremely high frequency satellites by entering into a fixed-price contract. Such procurement may also include—

subparagraph.content: material and equipment in economic order quantities when cost savings are achievable; and
cost reduction initiatives.

paragraph.heading: Use of incremental funding.—
paragraph.content: With respect to a contract entered into under paragraph (1) for the procurement of advanced extremely high frequency satellites, the Secretary may use incremental funding for a period not to exceed six fiscal years.

paragraph.heading: Liability.—
paragraph.content: A contract entered into under paragraph (1) shall provide that any obligation of the United States to make a payment under the contract is subject to the availability of appropriations for that purpose, and that the total liability to the Government for termination of any contract entered into shall be limited to the total amount of funding obligated at the time of termination.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.content: Except as provided by subsection (c), and excluding amounts described in paragraph (2), the total amount obligated or expended for the procurement of two advanced extremely high frequency satellites authorized by subsection (a) may not exceed $3,100,000,000.

paragraph.heading: Exclusion.—
paragraph.chapeau: The amounts described in this paragraph are amounts associated with the following:

subparagraph.content: Plans.
Technical data packages.
Post-delivery and program support costs.
Technical support for obsolescence studies.

subsection.heading: Waiver and Adjustment to Limitation Amount.—

paragraph.heading: Waiver.—
paragraph.content: In accordance with paragraph (2), the Secretary may waive the limitation in subsection (b)(1) if the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees written notification of the adjustment made to the amount set forth in such subsection.

paragraph.heading: Adjustment.—
paragraph.chapeau: Upon waiving the limitation under paragraph (1), the Secretary may adjust the amount set forth in subsection (b)(1) by the following:

subparagraph.content: The amounts of increases or decreases in costs attributable to economic inflation after September 30, 2011.
The amounts of increases or decreases in costs attributable to compliance with changes in Federal, State, or local laws enacted after September 30, 2011.

subparagraph.chapeau: The amounts of increases or decreases in costs of the satellites that are attributable to insertion of new technology into an advanced extremely high frequency satellite, as compared to the technology built into such a satellite procured prior to fiscal year 2012, if the Secretary determines, and certifies to the congressional defense committees, that insertion of the new technology is—

clause.content: expected to decrease the life-cycle cost of the satellite; or
required to meet an emerging threat that poses grave harm to national security.

subsection.heading: Use of Funds Available for Space Vehicle Number 5 for Space Vehicle Number 6.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may obligate and expend amounts authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2012 by section 101 for procurement for the Air Force as specified in the funding table in section 4101 and available for the advanced procurement of long-lead parts and the replacement of obsolete parts for advanced extremely high frequency satellite space vehicle number 5 for the advanced procurement of long-lead parts and the replacement of obsolete parts for advanced extremely high frequency satellite space vehicle number 6.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 30 days after the date on which the Secretary awards a contract under subsection (a), the Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on such contract, including the following:

paragraph.content: The total cost savings resulting from the authority provided by subsection (a).
The type and duration of the contract awarded.
The total contract value.
The funding profile by year.
The terms of the contract regarding the treatment of changes by the Federal Government to the requirements of the contract, including how any such changes may affect the success of the contract.

paragraph.chapeau: A plan for using cost savings described in paragraph (1) to improve the capability of military satellite communications, including a description of—

subparagraph.content: the available funds, by year, resulting from such cost savings;
the specific activities or subprograms to be funded by such cost savings and the funds, by year, allocated to each such activity or subprogram;
the objectives for each such activity or subprogram and the criteria used by the Secretary to determine which such activity or subprogram to fund;
the method in which such activities or subprograms will be awarded, including whether it will be on a competitive basis; and
the process for determining how and when such activities and subprograms would transition to an existing program or be established as a new program of record.

subsection.heading: Sense of Congress.—
subsection.content: It is the sense of Congress that the Secretary should not enter into a fixed-price contract under subsection (a) for the procurement of two advanced extremely high frequency satellites unless the Secretary determines that entering into such a contract will save the Air Force not less than 20 percent over the cost of procuring two such satellites separately.

section.heading: LIMITATION ON AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS FOR ACQUISITION OF JOINT TACTICAL RADIO SYSTEM.

subsection.heading: Limitation.—
subsection.content: Of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2012 for other procurement, Army, for covered programs of the joint tactical radio system, not more than 70 percent may be obligated or expended until the date on which the Secretary of the Army submits to the congressional defense committees written certification that the acquisition strategy for the full-rate production of covered programs of such radio system includes full and open competition (as defined in section 2302(3)(D) of title 10, United States Code) that includes commercially developed systems that the Secretary determines are qualified with respect to successful testing by the Army and certification by the National Security Agency.

subsection.heading: LRIP.—
subsection.content: The limitation under subsection (a) shall not apply to the low-rate initial production of covered programs.

subsection.heading: Covered Programs.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section, the term “covered programs” means, with respect to the joint tactical radio system, the following:

paragraph.content: The ground mobile radio.
The handheld, manpack, and small form fit.

section.heading: LIMITATION ON AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS FOR AVIATION FOREIGN INTERNAL DEFENSE PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: Limitation.—
subsection.content: Of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2012 for the procurement of fixed-wing non-standard aviation aircraft in support of the aviation foreign internal defense program, not more than 50 percent may be obligated or expended until the date that is 30 days after the date on which the Commander of the United States Special Operations Command submits the report under subsection (b)(1).

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.content: Not later than March 15, 2012, the Commander of the United States Special Operations Command shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the aviation foreign internal defense program.

paragraph.heading: Matters included.—
paragraph.chapeau: The report under paragraph (1) shall include the following:

subparagraph.content: An overall description of the program, including its goals and proposed metrics of performance success.
The results of any analysis of alternatives and efficiencies reviews for contracts awarded for the aviation foreign internal defense program.

An assessment of the advantages and disadvantages of procuring new aircraft, procuring used aircraft, or leasing aircraft to meet mission requirements, including an explanation of any efficiencies and savings.

A comprehensive strategy outlining and justifying the overall projected growth of the aviation foreign internal defense program to satisfy the increased requirements of the commanders of the geographic combatant commands.
An examination of efficiencies that could be gained by procuring platforms such as those being procured for light mobility aircraft.

paragraph.heading: Form.—
paragraph.content: The report under paragraph (1) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.

section.heading: F-35 JOINT STRIKE FIGHTER AIRCRAFT.
section.chapeau: In entering into a contract for the procurement of aircraft for the sixth and all subsequent low-rate initial production contract lots for the F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter aircraft, the Secretary of Defense shall ensure each of the following:

paragraph.content: That the contract is a fixed-price contract.
That the contract requires the contractor to assume full responsibility for costs under the contract above the target cost specified in the contract.

section.heading: ADDITIONAL OVERSIGHT REQUIREMENTS FOR THE UNDERSEA MOBILITY ACQUISITION PROGRAM OF THE UNITED STATES SPECIAL OPERATIONS COMMAND.

subsection.heading: Limitation on Milestone B Decision.—
subsection.chapeau: The Commander of the United States Special Operations Command may not make any milestone B acquisition decisions with respect to a covered element until a 30-day period has elapsed after the date on which the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment—

paragraph.content: conducts the assessment and determination under subsection (b) for the covered element; and

paragraph.chapeau: submits to the congressional defense committees a report including—

subparagraph.content: the determination of the Under Secretary with respect to the appropriate acquisition category for the covered element; and
the validated requirements, independent cost estimate, test and evaluation master plan, and technology readiness assessment described in paragraphs (1) through (4) of subsection (b), respectively.

subsection.heading: Assessment and Determination.—
subsection.chapeau: With respect to each covered element, the Under Secretary shall conduct an assessment and determination of whether to treat the covered element as a major defense acquisition program. Such assessment shall include—

paragraph.content: a requirements validation by the Joint Requirements Oversight Council or the Joint Capabilities Integration and Development system;
an independent cost estimate prepared by the Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation, or other comparable and qualified entity selected by the Director;
a test and evaluation master plan reviewed by the Director of Operational Test and Evaluation; and
a technology readiness assessment reviewed by the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Commander shall develop a plan consisting of a technology roadmap for undersea mobility capabilities that includes the following:

subparagraph.content: A description of the current capabilities provided by covered elements as of the date of the plan.
An identification and description of the requirements of the Commander for future undersea mobility platforms.
An identification of resources necessary to fulfill the requirements identified in subparagraph (B).
A description of the technology readiness levels of any covered element currently under development as of the date of the plan.
An identification of any potential gaps or projected shortfall in capability, along with steps to mitigate any such gap or shortfall.
Any other matters the Commander determines appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Submission.—
paragraph.content: The Commander shall submit to the congressional defense committees the plan under paragraph (1) at the same time as the Under Secretary submits the first report under subsection (a)(2) following the date of the enactment of the Carl Levin and Howard P. ‘Buck’ McKeon National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2015.

subsection.heading: Covered Element Defined.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section, the term “covered element” means any of the following elements of the undersea mobility acquisition program of the United States Special Operations Command:

paragraph.content: The dry combat submersible-light program.
The dry combat submersible-medium program.
The next-generation submarine shelter program.
Any new dry combat submersible developed under the undersea mobility acquisition program of the United States Special Operations Command after the date of the enactment of this Act.

section.heading: INCLUSION OF INFORMATION ON APPROVED COMBAT MISSION REQUIREMENTS IN QUARTERLY REPORTS ON USE OF COMBAT MISSION REQUIREMENT FUNDS.
section.content:
Section 123(b) of the Ike Skelton National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011 (Public Law 111-383; 124 Stat. 4159; 10 U.S.C. 167 note) is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraphs:
“(6) A table setting forth the Combat Mission Requirements approved during the fiscal year in which such report is submitted and the two preceding fiscal years, including for each such Requirement—
“(A) the title of such Requirement;
“(B) the date of approval of such Requirement; and
“(C) the amount of funding approved for such Requirement, and the source of such approved funds.
“(7) A statement of the amount of any unspent Combat Mission Requirements funds from the fiscal year in which such report is submitted and the two preceding fiscal years.” .

section.heading: JOINT SURVEILLANCE TARGET ATTACK RADAR SYSTEM AIRCRAFT RE-ENGINING PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: Report on Audit of Funds for Program.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Air Force Audit Agency shall submit to the congressional defense committees the results of a financial audit of the funds previously authorized and appropriated for the Joint Surveillance Target Attack Radar System (JSTARS) aircraft re-engining program.

paragraph.heading: Elements.—
paragraph.chapeau: The report on the audit required by paragraph (1) shall include the following:

subparagraph.chapeau: A description of how the funds described in that paragraph were expended, including—

clause.content: an assessment of the existence, completeness, and cost of the assets acquired with such funds; and

an assessment of the costs that were capitalized as military equipment and inventory and the cost characterized as operating expenses (including payroll, freight and shipment, inspection, and other operating costs).

subparagraph.content: A statement of the amount of such funds that remain in the original budget lines.
A statement of the amount of such funds that were reprogrammed or expired, and in which accounts.

subsection.heading: Use of Funds.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Air Force shall take appropriate actions to ensure that funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act for JSTARS aircraft, and any funds described by subsection (a)(2)(B), are obligated and expended for the purposes for which authorized and appropriated, including, but not limited to, the installation of one engine shipset on an operational JSTARS aircraft.

section.heading: AUTHORITY FOR EXCHANGE WITH UNITED KINGDOM OF SPECIFIED F-35 LIGHTNING II JOINT STRIKE FIGHTER AIRCRAFT.

paragraph.heading: Exchange authority.—
paragraph.content: In accordance with subsection (c), the Secretary of Defense may transfer to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (in this section referred to as the “United Kingdom”) all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to an aircraft described in paragraph (2) in exchange for the transfer by the United Kingdom to the United States of all right, title, and interest of the United Kingdom in and to an aircraft described in paragraph (3). The Secretary may execute the exchange under this section on behalf of the United States only with the concurrence of the Secretary of State.

paragraph.heading: Aircraft to be exchanged by united states.—
paragraph.content: The aircraft authorized to be transferred by the United States under this subsection is an F-35 Lightning II aircraft in the Carrier Variant configuration acquired by the United States for the Marine Corps under a future Joint Strike Fighter program contract referred to as the Low-Rate Initial Production 6 contract.

paragraph.heading: Aircraft to be exchanged by united kingdom.—
paragraph.content: The aircraft for which the exchange under paragraph (1) may be made is an F-35 Lightning II aircraft in the Short-Take Off and Vertical Landing configuration that, as of November 19, 2010, is being acquired on behalf of the United Kingdom under an existing Joint Strike Fighter program contract referred to as the Low-Rate Initial Production 4 contract.

paragraph.heading: Funding sources for aircraft to be exchanged by united states.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Except as provided in subparagraph (B), funds for production of the aircraft to be transferred by the United States (including the propulsion system, long lead-time materials, the production build, and deficiency corrections) may be derived from appropriations for Aircraft Procurement, Navy, for the aircraft under the contract referred to in subsection (a)(2).

subparagraph.heading: Exception.—
subparagraph.content: Costs for flight test instrumentation of the aircraft to be transferred by the United States and any other non-recurring and recurring costs for that aircraft associated with unique requirements of the United Kingdom may not be borne by the United States.

paragraph.heading: Funding sources for aircraft to be exchanged by united kingdom.—
paragraph.content: Costs for upgrades and modifications of the aircraft to be transferred to the United States that are necessary to bring that aircraft to the Low-Rate Initial Production 6 configuration under the contract referred to in subsection (a)(2) may not be borne by the United States.

subsection.heading: Implementation.—
subsection.content: The exchange under this section shall be implemented pursuant to the memorandum of understanding titled “Joint Strike Fighter Production, Sustainment, and Follow-on Development Memorandum of Understanding”, which entered into effect among nine nations including the United States and the United Kingdom on December 31, 2006, consistent with section 27 of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2767), and as supplemented as necessary by the United States and the United Kingdom.

section.heading: REPORT ON PROBATIONARY PERIOD IN DEVELOPMENT OF SHORT TAKE-OFF, VERTICAL LANDING VARIANT OF THE JOINT STRIKE FIGHTER.
section.chapeau: Not later than 45 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the development of the short take-off, vertical landing variant of the Joint Strike Fighter (otherwise known as the F-35B Joint Strike Fighter) that includes the following:

paragraph.content: An identification of the criteria that the Secretary determines must be satisfied before the F-35B Joint Strike Fighter can be removed from the two-year probationary status imposed by the Secretary on or about January 6, 2011.

paragraph.chapeau: A mid-probationary period assessment of—

subparagraph.content: the performance of the F-35B Joint Strike Fighter based on the criteria described in paragraph (1); and
the technical issues that remain in the development program for the F-35B Joint Strike Fighter.

paragraph.content: A plan for how the Secretary intends to resolve the issues described in paragraph (2)(B) before January 6, 2013.

section.heading: REPORT ON PLAN TO IMPLEMENT WEAPON SYSTEMS ACQUISITION REFORM ACT OF 2009 MEASURES WITHIN THE JOINT STRIKE FIGHTER AIRCRAFT PROGRAM.
section.chapeau: At the same time the budget of the President for fiscal year 2013 is submitted to Congress pursuant to section 1105 of title 31, United States Code, the Under Secretary for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a report on the plans of the Department of Defense to implement the requirements of the Weapon Systems Acquisition Reform Act of 2009 (Public Law 111-23), and the amendments made by that Act, within the Joint Strike Fighter (JSF) aircraft program. The report shall set forth the following:

paragraph.content: Specific goals for implementing the requirements of the Weapon Systems Acquisition Reform Act of 2009, and the amendments made by that Act, within the Joint Strike Fighter aircraft program.
A schedule for achieving each goal set forth under paragraph (1) for the Joint Strike Fighter aircraft program.
